CLOSING on Gerrit change 1132 (commit c1fc3cee4): Verified +1 and submittable=True. The LLM-Review
label still shows an aggregate -1 from an earlier fail-closed infra veto
("[LLM-Review: BLOCK - coverage-gap (review-error)]", explicitly "infrastructure, not your code"),
but the re-triggered review PASSED and the submit requirement resolves on max value, so
/changes/1132?o=SUBMITTABLE returns True. Recording that because the aggregate label is misleading
here; the submit requirement is the authority.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, each with evidence:

- temperature WITHDRAWN when caps.supports_temperature is False and RETAINED when True:
  test_temperature_is_withdrawn_for_a_model_measured_to_reject_it and
  test_temperature_is_retained_when_the_model_supports_it. The retention test is the negative
  control that stops a blanket withdrawal passing.
- a per-request output cap only RAISES the floor:
  test_a_per_request_output_cap_raises_but_never_lowers_the_floor, plus
  test_an_explicit_output_token_limit_clamps_with_a_floor_of_256 for the one knob that may reduce.
- a per-request step budget only raises: test_a_per_request_step_budget_raises_but_never_lowers and
  test_an_explicit_iteration_limit_clamps_with_a_floor_of_2.
- build_model_settings performs NO side effect:
  test_building_settings_has_no_side_effect_on_the_dedup_set asserts
  runner._TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED is untouched after a withdrawal. The .add() and logger.info
  stay at runner.py:418-423; the builder only omits the key. The leaf rule
  (test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner) passes.
- module sizes: structured_run.py 373 -> 477, inside its own 100 <= loc < 500 guard. NOTE only 23
  lines of headroom remain; task 5e75 targets the same module and should plan a second themed
  module rather than piling on.
- runner.py under 700 on THIS commit: 699 -> 647, recorded in the commit message in the greppable
  form the AC requires (`runner.py before: 699` / `runner.py after: 647`), verifiable with
  `git log -1 --format=%B c1fc3cee4 | grep -E 'runner\.py (before|after): [0-9]+'`.
- seam guard covers the new move: build_model_settings and build_usage_limits added to BOTH
  hardcoded lists in test_structured_run_seam.py, so the guard asserts something about them rather
  than silently passing.
- monkeypatch repoints: none needed. effective_max_iterations/effective_max_tokens stay re-exported
  from runner.py because test_llm_failure_matrix.py and test_plan_review_verify_recovery.py import
  them from rebar.llm.runner.

HELD-OUT TDD: 14 tests authored and confirmed RED (the seam did not exist); the implementer was
given ONLY the 2 happy-path tests, with the other 12 physically removed from its tree. All 14 passed
on restore. THREE MUTATIONS each caught by a held-out test: always-send-temperature (withdrawal
test), alias cache_settings instead of copying (8 failures incl. the aliasing test), and returning
req_limit in place of eff_max_iter (the non-invertibility test). So the assertions have teeth.

THE PLAN GATE EARNED ITS KEEP HERE - four review rounds, four real defects, none cosmetic:
  R1 my own AC had NO ORACLE ("LOC recorded in the commit message" is a process obligation
     satisfiable without measuring). Split into a machine-enforced end-state plus a greppable record.
  R2a `cache_settings` was missing from the signature. It is computed at runner.py:381 as
      `None if self._model_override else cache_settings_for(caps)`. Recomputing it inside the
      builder would have DROPPED the model_override guard and silently re-enabled cache settings on
      the offline TestModel path - a live regression, not a style issue.
  R2b the seam guard's hardcoded lists would not have covered the new symbols.
  R3 `-> tuple` never named its contents. eff_max_iter is NOT recoverable from the UsageLimits it
     builds: only max(8, eff_max_iter) is stored as tool_calls_limit and max() cannot be inverted,
     so for eff_max_iter <= 8 the original is gone. Pinned to tuple[UsageLimits, int, int].

VERIFICATION: full suite 8253 passed / 74 skipped / 0 FAILED; make lint 0; make typecheck 0.
